title: Periodic Assumption Edge Discontinuity
description: Three repeated copies of a captured frame showing whether the signal joins at the boundaries, with the resulting clean or leaked spectrum below.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Spectral Leakage
Windowing
chapter_title: Windowing, Spectral Leakage, and Peak Detection

learningObjectives: Interpret the DFT's implicit periodic-repetition assumption
Explain why a fractional cycle count creates an edge discontinuity
Attribute leakage to the boundary rather than to the signal
prerequisites: The DFT operates on a finite frame
A spectrum is magnitude per bin

controls.label: Snap to whole cycles
controls.purpose: Jump to the nearest integer cycle count

simulationModel.modelType: Live 64-point DFT of a synthesized frame
assumptions: N = 64 with a single sinusoid and a fixed non-zero starting phase
limitations: Shows the untapered case only; window functions are covered in the companion sim

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Make the hidden assumption visible, then show its consequence
keyQuestions: Do the repeated copies join smoothly?
Did the signal change, or only where the frame cut it?
commonMisconceptions: That leakage is a property of the signal rather than of the frame boundary
assessmentOpportunities: Give evidence that observed leakage is not noise
